::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** April 5th 1895  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne  
**Manuscript:** MS Hampshire Record Office 67M92W/82/24
:::

Dear [Mr Wooldridge](people/person_2094.qmd)
I am afraid I am very ignorant about the term of the loan of the £1000.  I cannot say I ever expect [Mrs Yonge](people/person_1604.qmd) to pay it back to me.  She does not even know that I have paid it off.

If I discontinue the payment for insuring her life, will the future payment of £1000 on her death lapse.

Or if I continue it, or my heirs (for I can hardly expect to survive her) will it be paid on her death to my heirs?

Also, to whom for the future shall I pay the fire insurance 1st for the London houses  2nd for those at Otterbourne?

Apologising for all the trouble I am giving
Yours truly
C M Yonge
